summary: Added rules A1-A6 to docs/agent-contracts.md in its existing terse normative style and raised the contract's doc budget line from 200 to 220 in scripts/check-docs.sh (A7, required because the new enforced rules push the contract past 200 lines): new 'Corrective and re-derivation tasks' section (post-re-derivation sweep of docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md, docs/release/build-and-release.md, the release changelog and ADR implementation notes with superseded marking and a never-current superseded hash; no full artifact/live/security re-derivation while a corrective set is open absent a consolidated adversarial review clearing BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM or explicit user acceptance; corrective work continues the single-dotted task-ID sequence); new 'Invocation and evidence integrity' section (attempt-0 with absent report retried and recorded as retried; destructive pre-fix probes in an isolated export or worktree and no-build results valid only after a rebuild when the tree may have been touched; causal procedure claims checked against pinned-host research or source with disproved attributions withdrawn or superseded); tightened 'Where reports go' rule 5 (base report for every kind that exists for the task and every preserved .attempt-<n>.json on disk for every kind the reports array lists, not only reviewer-report.json); new 'Phase gate obligations' section (explicit fix-now / accept-with-register-entry / defer-with-rationale disposition, the user owning the accept, for every new security finding before the next phase starts; an open finding without a recorded disposition is a gate defect); two Enforcement-scope entries ('from phase 20' reports-array attempts and 'from phase 26' subagents/aggregate consistency with phases before 26 not rewritten) plus the statement that scripts/check-agents.sh enforces both and fails if its scope constants disagree with this section; and the release-phase gate precedent (Phase 14 and Phase 21) in 'Phase-level orchestration record'. docs/agent-contracts.md is 218 lines against the 220 target. No state.json, PLANS.md, docs/planning/**, scripts/check-agents.sh, goal/DG/ADR, product code, test, artifact, or manifest change; no commit or tag.
validation: wc -l docs/agent-contracts.md -> 218 (at or below the 220 target); scripts/check-docs.sh:98 -> 'budget docs/agent-contracts.md 220' (was 200).
source /config/arrtags-env.sh && bash scripts/check-docs.sh -> exit 0, 'check-docs: PASS', all nine sections ok including 'ok: doc budget checked' and 'ok: agent report contracts conform'.

bash scripts/check-agents.sh -> exit 0, 'check-agents: PASS', all twelve sections ok including 'ok: contract enforcement scope agrees with the script' (the existing APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20 self-check), 'ok: per-agent default path and status enum agree with the contract', 'ok: worker/reviewer report pairing checked', and 'ok: plan state lists the review evidence'.

Sensitivity probe (budget validator): with scripts/check-docs.sh temporarily set back to the old 'budget docs/agent-contracts.md 200', check-docs exits 1 with exactly 'FAIL: docs/agent-contracts.md is 218 lines (budget 200)' and 'check-docs: FAIL'; restoring 220 exits 0 with 'check-docs: PASS'. Probe output was captured under /tmp/26.2/ (removed after the task).

Sensitivity probe (existing enforcement-scope self-check): with 'from phase 20' temporarily replaced by 'from phase twenty' in docs/agent-contracts.md, check-agents exits 1 with exactly 'FAIL: APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20 is not stated in docs/agent-contracts.md (Enforcement scope)' and 'check-agents: FAIL'; the file was then restored byte-identical (cmp clean) and check-agents exits 0 'check-agents: PASS'. This shows the new 'from phase 26' bullet does not displace or break the phase-20 marker the current script greps.

git diff --numstat -> docs/agent-contracts.md 48 insertions / 4 deletions; scripts/check-docs.sh 1 insertion / 1 deletion. git diff --check clean. git status --short before this report existed showed only ' M docs/agent-contracts.md' and ' M scripts/check-docs.sh'.

Content presence check over docs/agent-contracts.md: A1 section lines 51-63; A2 section lines 65-74; A3 rule 5 lines 20-25; A4 section lines 102-107; A5 entries lines 148-157 and the script statement lines 156-157; A6 bullet lines 121-123; the unchanged Enforcement-scope sentence naming APPLIES_FROM_PHASE at line 130. Searches confirm the old rule-5 wording ('lists at minimum its') is absent from the contract and the old budget value ('budget docs/agent-contracts.md 200') is absent repo-wide.

Post-persistence transient run, after docs/implementation/26.2/worker-report.json existed and before the orchestrator's 26.2 reviewer report exists/listed: bash scripts/check-agents.sh exits 1 with exactly 'FAIL: task 26.2 has a worker report but no reviewer report (add an exemption only if covered)' and 'FAIL: task 26.2 has a reviewer report on disk but docs/plan/state.json does not list it in reports' ('check-agents: FAIL'); bash scripts/check-docs.sh exits 1 in section 9 mirroring those two lines ('check-docs: FAIL') while its other eight sections are ok, including 'ok: doc budget checked'. jq empty docs/implementation/26.2/worker-report.json exits 0 (report is valid JSON). The pre-report runs above are the authoritative PASS results.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A1 is present: after any artifact re-derivation, the named current-state surfaces (docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md, docs/release/build-and-release.md, the release changelog, ADR implementation notes) are swept for the superseded artifact identity and each occurrence marked superseded; a superseded hash is never presented as current; a release candidate with an open corrective set does not begin a full artifact/live/security re-derivation until a consolidated adversarial review clears BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM or the user accepts re-running; corrective work continues the single-dotted task-ID sequence.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/agent-contracts.md lines 51-63 ('## Corrective and re-derivation tasks'), three bullets covering exactly those three rules.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A2 is present: an attempt-0 invocation whose report is absent on disk is retried before being treated as an outcome and recorded as retried; destructive pre-fix probes run in an isolated export or worktree, never the shared tree, and a no-build test result is valid after a rebuild when another agent may have touched the tree; a causal procedure finding is checked against the pinned-host research or source before entering a canonical procedure document, and a disproved attribution is recorded as withdrawn or superseded.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/agent-contracts.md lines 65-74 ('## Invocation and evidence integrity'), three bullets covering exactly those three rules.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A3 tightens 'Where reports go' rule 5 so the reports array lists every preserved .attempt-<n>.json for every report kind it lists (not only reviewer-report.json), as well as the base report for each kind that exists.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/agent-contracts.md lines 20-25: 'the base report for every kind that exists for the task, and every preserved `.attempt-<n>.json` on disk for every kind it lists (not only `reviewer-report.json`)'; the old 'lists at minimum its reviewer-report.json' wording is absent (grep).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A4 is present: at each phase gate the orchestrator records an explicit disposition (fix-now / accept-with-register-entry / defer-with-rationale, the user owning an accept) for every new security finding the phase raised, before the next phase starts; an open finding without a recorded disposition is a gate defect.

A5 adds both enforceable entries: from phase 20 the reports array lists every on-disk preserved .attempt-<n>.json for each listed report kind plus each existing kind's base report; from phase 26 a phase-level orchestration record carries subagents and an aggregate whose numeric fields equal sums recomputed from the task-level records, with phases before 26 stated as predating the rule and not rewritten; and states that scripts/check-agents.sh enforces both and fails if its scope constants disagree with the section.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/agent-contracts.md lines 148-150 ('from phase 20' reports-array entry), lines 151-154 ('from phase 26' subagents/aggregate entry including 'Phases before 26 predate this rule and are not rewritten.'), lines 156-157 ('scripts/check-agents.sh enforces both rules and fails if its scope constants disagree with the phases stated here.').

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A6 adds one sentence to 'Phase-level orchestration record': a release phase may use the release review as its gate (the Phase 14 and Phase 21 precedent), in which case phase_review and phase_review_status point at the release review and there is no separate phase-reviewer record.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/agent-contracts.md lines 121-123: a single-sentence bullet with the Phase 14 and Phase 21 precedent, the two pointer fields, and the absent separate phase-reviewer record.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A7: the docs/agent-contracts.md budget line in scripts/check-docs.sh is raised only because the new content requires it, and scripts/check-docs.sh passes including the budget check.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: scripts/check-docs.sh:98 'budget docs/agent-contracts.md 220' (was 200); 218-line file exceeds the old 200 budget; 'ok: doc budget checked' and 'check-docs: PASS' at exit 0; sensitivity probe shows the budget check fails at 200 and passes at 220.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The contract still states the existing APPLIES_FROM_PHASE rule, and the new 'from phase 26' wording does not contradict or break the current check-agents.sh self-check (which does not yet know a 26 constant; task 26.3 adds it).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/agent-contracts.md line 130 retains 'The script fails if this number and its own `APPLIES_FROM_PHASE` disagree.' and the 'from phase 20' bullets remain; check-agents reports 'ok: contract enforcement scope agrees with the script'; the temporary-substitution probe fails check-agents with 'FAIL: APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20 is not stated in docs/agent-contracts.md (Enforcement scope)' and passes after restore.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Task boundary respected: no goal, decision gate (DG-), ADR, or existing phase/gate text modified; no docs/plan/state.json, PLANS.md, docs/planning/**, or scripts/check-agents.sh change; no product code, test, artifact, or manifest change; no commit or tag.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: git status --short shows only ' M docs/agent-contracts.md' and ' M scripts/check-docs.sh' (plus the untracked docs/implementation/26.2/ report); git diff --numstat is 48/4 and 1/1 on exactly those two files; the check-docs.sh diff is the single budget line; the agent-contracts diff adds only the new sections, the tightened rule 5, the A5 bullets/statement, and the A6 bullet.

test_sensitivity: Budget validator (check-docs.sh section 7): setting the budget line temporarily back to the old 200 makes docs/agent-contracts.md fail with 'FAIL: docs/agent-contracts.md is 218 lines (budget 200)' and check-docs exit 1; restoring 220 makes it pass at exit 0. The guard genuinely reads the new value and rejects the pre-change budget.

Existing contract/script scope self-check (check-agents.sh): removing all 'from phase 20' markers from the contract (temporary substitution to 'from phase twenty') makes check-agents fail with 'FAIL: APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20 is not stated in docs/agent-contracts.md (Enforcement scope)'; the contract was restored byte-identical and check-agents passes. This confirms the A5 additions neither displaced nor disabled the existing rule, and that the marker the current script requires is still present.

No new production behaviour or test exists in this documentation-only task; the A3/A5 rules are prose, and their guard implementation is task 26.3 (per the phase plan), so no code-level sensitivity probe applies here. The two probes above are the guards this task touches.

surfaces: docs/agent-contracts.md - the normative agent-report contract; updated with A1-A6 and the tightened rule 5.
scripts/check-docs.sh - only the docs/agent-contracts.md budget line (200 -> 220); the surrounding budget comment is unchanged.

No canonical current-state surface needed updating: docs/plan/state.json, PLANS.md, docs/status.md, docs/changelog/, docs/limitations/, README.md, docs/architecture/, and docs/data-model/ carry no status/capability/configuration/limitation fact this change alters, and the task boundary forbids touching plan state.
old_values_removed: scripts/check-docs.sh budget value 200 for docs/agent-contracts.md: repo-wide search for 'budget docs/agent-contracts.md 200' is empty; line 98 now reads 220.

Old 'Where reports go' rule 5 wording 'A task with a `worker-report.json` lists at minimum its `reviewer-report.json` ...': search for 'lists at minimum its' in docs/agent-contracts.md is empty; replaced by the tightened base-report/every-attempt wording.

known_limitations: Exact behaviour: with docs/implementation/26.2/worker-report.json on disk and no docs/implementation/26.2/reviewer-report.json and no 26.2 listing in docs/plan/state.json reports, scripts/check-agents.sh fails exactly the two contract-defined pairing lines for task 26.2 ('FAIL: task 26.2 has a worker report but no reviewer report (add an exemption only if covered)' and 'FAIL: task 26.2 has a reviewer report on disk but docs/plan/state.json does not list it in reports') and scripts/check-docs.sh section 9 mirrors them (exit 1) while its other eight sections are ok including the doc budget. Precondition: the orchestrator has not yet written the 26.2 review report and listed it. Consequence: the authoritative PASS runs recorded above were taken before this report existed; the interim state clears when the orchestrator writes the review report and lists it in reports. This is the same transient state tasks 20.3, 21.4/21.9/21.13, and 26.1 recorded; no exemption or workaround was applied.

Until task 26.3 lands, the A5 sentences 'from phase 20' (attempts listing) and 'from phase 26' (subagents/aggregate sums) describe rules the current scripts/check-agents.sh does not yet enforce: its only scope constant is APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20 and its state-reports check only requires some reviewer-report entry. The delegation directed that the contract state the script enforces both, and 26.3 owns installing both guards and the phase-26 constant with its self-check; between 26.2 and 26.3 the contract states the target enforcement state rather than the script's current checks.

The budget raise to 220 leaves 2 lines of headroom above the current 218; any later contract growth beyond those 2 lines must again be accompanied by an actually enforced rule, per the unchanged budget comment in scripts/check-docs.sh.

The tightened rule 5 replaces the explicit kind enumeration (reviewer/test-quality/security/live-verification) with 'the base report for every kind that exists for the task'; this is at least as strong as the old wording. The 26.3 attempts guard, as scoped, checks every preserved .attempt-<n>.json for each report kind already listed, so no guard semantics depend on the enumeration.

interpretations.question: Which value should the docs/agent-contracts.md budget line carry now that the contract is 218 lines?
interpretations.chosen: 220, the ceiling the delegation states, rather than the exact 218.
interpretations.basis: The delegation permits raising the budget only for the A3/A5 enforced rules and says to budget the prose so the contract ends at or below 220 lines; the check-docs comment requires the raise to accompany an actually enforced rule, which A3/A5 are (task 26.3).
interpretations.impact: Two lines of headroom before another raise would be required; the check itself passes at 218 <= 220.

interpretations.question: How should rule 5 name the report kinds whose base reports must be listed, now that the enumeration is replaced by a general rule?
interpretations.chosen: 'the base report for every kind that exists for the task' plus 'every preserved .attempt-<n>.json on disk for every kind it lists (not only reviewer-report.json)'.
interpretations.basis: The delegation's A3 wording ('as well as the base report for each kind that exists') and the requirement to generalize attempts beyond reviewer-report.json.
interpretations.impact: The contract is at least as strong as the old enumeration (reviewer, test-quality, security, live-verification); the 26.3 guard checks attempts for kinds already listed, so its behaviour is unchanged by this wording.

interpretations.question: Where should the new sections sit in the contract?
interpretations.chosen: A1 and A2 after 'Shared enums'; A4 after 'Phase review gate conformance'; A6 as a bullet in 'Phase-level orchestration record'; A5 at the end of the Enforcement-scope bullet list.
interpretations.basis: Keeps related rules adjacent (integrity rules together, gate obligations next to gate conformance, enforcement bullets next to the scope constants they describe).
interpretations.impact: Presentation only; no rule text or semantics depend on section order.
